This task is straightforward and observable: the player needs to find and break a dark_oak_slab block in the environment. It requires no deep Minecraft domain knowledge beyond knowing how to break blocks (left-click/attack). It is easily verifiable by checking if the player has picked up a dark_oak_slab item in their inventory. The scene can be designed with dark_oak_slabs placed in a visible, accessible location.

milestones.description: Uses inventory_has because when a player mines (breaks) a dark_oak_slab block, the slab item drops and is automatically picked up into their inventory. Dark oak slabs are wooden blocks that always drop themselves when mined (no tool required). The player starts with an empty inventory, so any dark_oak_slab presence confirms successful mining. This is the preferred rule type for mine tasks per the mapping guidelines.

scene_description: A cleared grass platform (11x11) in a dark oak forest with a 2x2 patch of dark_oak_slabs placed at ground level, easily visible and accessible. A dark oak planks pillar serves as a visual landmark. The player spawns 3-4 blocks from the slabs.
task_text: Mine a dark oak slab from the small platform on the ground nearby.
design_notes: The scene places 4 dark_oak_slabs in a 2x2 patch at (~2,~0,~3) to (~3,~0,~4), about 3-4 blocks from spawn. The area above is cleared to remove tree canopy and improve visibility. A 2-tall dark_oak_planks pillar at (~-2,~0,~4) serves as a landmark but won't confuse the mining task (planks ≠ slabs). The player needs no tools — wooden slabs break by hand in ~3 seconds. Multiple slabs provide redundancy in case one is hard to target.
